A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TESSERA work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison despite the changed title, organization, and layout.

before.justification: V2 reports original crop classification, canopy height, biomass, fire, and stocking-index results, together with scaling experiments and component ablations.

after.justification: V5 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative fire classification, label-efficiency evaluation, and training diagnostics.

M1.justification: The dual Sentinel encoders, 128-dimensional fusion, quantization, Barlow Twins plus mixup objective, and inference procedure are retained. V5 clarifies the projector as four hidden layers plus input/output layers; identical parameter counts support a documentation correction rather than an architecture change. Uniform mixup sampling is equivalent to v2's Beta(1,1).

E1.justification: The global pretraining coverage and five downstream datasets, regions, and tasks remain the same. Additional fire evaluations use the existing California areas. V5's 2020 fire dates already appear in v2 Appendix G, despite conflicting 2021 wording in v2's main text; this does not establish new temporal coverage.

E2.justification: V5 adds GSE and a task-specific pre/post-fire Sentinel-2 composite as evaluated comparators for burned-area classification (Figure 6, Appendix A.6). Comparator sets elsewhere are retained. In particular, GSE already appears in v2's biomass Figure 4 and Appendix H.

E3.justification: V5 adds a fire protocol with a fixed 20% test set, stratified label subsampling, and exclusion of ambiguous MTBS class 1. It also reports biomass clipping at 500 t/ha and revises stated settings: crop RF trees from 200 to 100, removal of the pretraining learning-rate plateau, and largest-projector batch size from 4,096 to 16,384. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V5 adds fire label-efficiency experiments and spatial false-positive/false-negative analysis (Figure 6), extending the earlier qualitative case study. New Figure 9 examines component losses, projector and embedding RankMe trajectories, and downstream performance during training. Existing component ablations and scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Crop standard deviations, 12 canopy training runs, and biomass averages and minimum-maximum ranges over five splits are retained. V5 Figure 7 adds shaded bands around stocking-index regression lines, but neither its caption nor Appendix A.8 defines them. Whether these constitute new uncertainty reporting, and how they were estimated, remains unclear.

E6.justification: V5 newly reports fire F1 above 0.96 and over 90% of final performance using 0.01% of training labels. Biomass curves and examples are revised alongside the clipping specification, with fuller GSE results; these are not same-setting performance gains over v2. The ETH stocking-index result changes from R2 0.413 and RMSE 32.5 Mg/ha to 0.424 and 31.9, beyond rounding. Crop, canopy, and component-ablation scores are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1-14 retain the d-pixel definitions, training losses, RankMe definition, and clustering metrics. Replacing Beta sampling with a uniform distribution is mathematically equivalent at v2's specified parameter value. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: V5 newly presents explicit FAIR compliance as a contribution in the title, introduction, and conclusion. The central claims about open, precomputed global 10 m embeddings, label efficiency, and performance across five downstream tasks remain.

C2.justification: V5 adds qualifications about MTBS reference disagreements, explains the biomass winner's prediction ceiling, and justifies canopy temporal stability through absence of logging or burning. It also reverses v2's GEDI mountainous-terrain unreliability statement with an unexplained 'does not,' introducing a wording ambiguity with scientific implications.

D1.justification: V5 adds fire RF hyperparameters and composite date windows, clarifies projector layers and activations, and documents version pinning and a daily Parquet index. It also discloses that BioMassters patch coordinates and years were obtained upon request. Existing code, weights, hardware descriptions, and GeoTessera access are largely retained.

R1.justification: V5 explicitly positions AlphaEarth as the closest alternative and cites its paper, while adding FAIR-related literature and MOSAIKS and SkySense++ entries to Table 5. Some introductory citations are removed. These are targeted updates to the existing research positioning, not a wholesale change.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and biomass and fire narratives are substantially rewritten. The overview becomes a Methods section, and the separate appendices are consolidated into Materials and Methods subsections. Terminology, explanations, and cross-references are extensively edited beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V5 adds global embedding visualizations and training-dynamics figures, substantially redesigns the biomass and fire figures, and redraws stocking-index plots with density colors and shaded bands. Typography, figure placement, captions, and table pagination also change broadly; several other figures are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The quantitative fire comparisons and documented evaluation protocol address a specific weakness of v2's largely qualitative fire evidence. Training diagnostics and clearer implementation and data-access information also improve assessability. These strengthen an already substantial empirical paper incrementally. The unexplained regression bands and reversed GEDI terrain caveat leave reporting ambiguities, while changed biomass preprocessing prevents interpreting revised scores as direct performance gains.
